steps.context: This is the primary answer to the research question. In a 2x2 design the question 'does the treatment effect differ between the two time points' is exactly the condition:time interaction coefficient — not a comparison of two independently thresholded DE lists. All contrasts come from the single model fitted in T1S1 so they share dispersion estimates and one multiple-testing frame.

constraints: The interaction Wald test (and the LRT) is the answer to the question — do NOT answer by intersecting or Venn-diagramming two separately thresholded per-timepoint DE lists, and say so in the report
All contrasts must be extracted from one fitted model so dispersions and the multiple-testing frame are shared
Use BH FDR; report both 0.05 and 0.1 thresholds rather than moving the threshold to find hits
Do not use shrunken LFCs for significance calls — shrinkage is for ranking and visualisation only
If apeglm cannot be applied to the interaction coefficient given the level coding, use ashr and state which was used
steps.description: Fit the DESeq2 negative-binomial GLM on the T1S1 object with design ~ condition + time + condition:time (Wald test). Extract, as the PRIMARY result, the condition:time interaction coefficient: log2 fold change, standard error, Wald statistic, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value for every retained gene, with independent filtering on. Additionally run a likelihood-ratio test of the full model against the reduced additive model ~ condition + time, and report the number of LRT-significant genes at FDR < 0.05 — this is the model-level statement of whether an interaction term is warranted. steps.question: Among genes with a condition:time interaction, is the treatment response amplified, dampened, reversed in sign, or present at only one of t0 and t1?

Class labels are descriptive only — do not present a class assignment as a statistical test result

plan.title: Treatment x time interaction DE in 2x2 bulk RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question — does the treatment effect differ between t0 and t1 — is a formal interaction question on a 2x2 factorial bulk RNA-seq design: 12 samples (12000 genes x 12 count columns in counts.csv, one gene-symbol column + 12 sample columns), 2 conditions x 2 time points (t0, t1), n=3 per cell, single batch, raw Salmon counts. The plan is deliberately short and centred on one statistical object: a DESeq2 negative-binomial GLM with design ~ condition + time + condition:time, where the interaction Wald test IS the answer. Everything else supports or interprets that test.

T1S1 builds the DESeq2 object, verifies that metadata.csv sample IDs align to the count matrix columns exactly, confirms the design is balanced 3/3/3/3, filters low-count genes, and produces VST-based QC (PCA, sample distances, dispersion) so that any outlier or swapped label is caught before inference rather than after. It also reports the size-factor range, since Salmon-derived gene counts occasionally carry non-integer artefacts that must be rounded, not silently coerced.

T1S2 is the primary inference: the interaction term, plus the simple treatment effects within each time point extracted by contrast from the same fitted model. This ordering matters — the honest answer to 'does the effect differ' is the interaction FDR, not a Venn diagram of two separate per-timepoint DE lists, which is the most common error in this design. The step is explicitly required to report the interaction result as the primary readout and to flag the power limitation: with n=3 per cell the interaction contrast has roughly half the effective power of a main effect, so few or zero interaction-significant genes is a plausible and reportable outcome, not a failed analysis. It also runs a likelihood-ratio test of the full model against the additive model ~ condition + time as a model-level check on whether an interaction is needed at all.

T1S3 characterises the shape of any interaction: classifying genes into amplified, dampened, reversed (sign flip) and time-specific response patterns using the shrunken per-timepoint log2 fold changes, so that a significant interaction is described mechanistically rather than only counted.

T2S1 runs enrichment on the interaction statistic. It is a separate track because it depends only on T1S2's ranked results and works on a generic ranked gene list; it uses the human hallmark and GO Biological Process gene sets confirmed present in the reference store (HGNC symbols, matching this matrix's gene-symbol index). Preranked GSEA on the interaction Wald statistic is preferred over over-representation of a thresholded list, precisely because the interaction list may be short. If the ranked interaction signal is empty or degenerate, the step should also rank on the per-timepoint contrasts and report the difference in enriched sets, stating clearly that this is a descriptive comparison and not a test of differential enrichment.

Limits stated up front: 12 samples, one batch, one cell line, no biological replication beyond the three wells per cell — this design supports a within-experiment statistical claim about interaction, not a generalisable one.
